assertion: According to a poll conducted by the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC) in April, 65% of 666 Baltimore City residents surveyed said they trust their local government “never” or “only some of the time.”
Only 41% believed that the city is headed in the right direction while 45% said the city is not progressing in the right direction. But, 61% of residents are optimistic about the future of the city.

Of the same polled residents, 61% said they have “a lot” or “some” trust in local news organizations, stating that the coverage is accurate and fair. Conversely, 38% of residents said they had little to no trust of news organizations at all.

A 2025 poll of 628 Baltimore County residents by UMBC found that 42% of county residents polled said improvement of public safety would encourage them to visit Baltimore City. 19% said nothing would encourage them to visit.
As for news consumption, a 2025 UMBC poll found that 42% of city residents polled received their news from The Baltimore Sun and 53% from Fox45.
independent_value: 42% Sun, 53% Fox45; the poll asks whether respondents have consumed each outlet, not a primary source
